outcome: No event dated inside the window settles the question. The result that answers it negatively, as a relative-consistency statement, is Asperó and Golshani's arXiv preprint of 20 September 2018 (revised to v7 on 24 April 2024, inside the window): from a weakly compact cardinal they force GCH together with no ℵ2-Souslin trees. I found no journal publication, public verification or erratum for it, and the Wikipedia Suslin tree article still calls the question a longstanding open problem; the in-window Rinot–Yadai–You preprint (v2, 29 February 2024) also says the existence of ℵ2-Souslin trees 'remain[s] open to this date'.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the statement alone, before weighing any event. (a) The hypothesis: the generalized continuum hypothesis, GCH (2^κ = κ⁺ for the infinite cardinals κ; the statement names no restriction, so all infinite κ). (b) The conclusion: the existence of an ℵ2-Suslin tree, i.e. a tree of height ω2 whose levels have size below ℵ2 (an ℵ2-tree) with no branch of length ℵ2 and no antichain of size ℵ2. (c) The relation asked about: whether GCH implies (is ZFC-provably followed by) that conclusion. A positive answer is a ZFC proof from GCH alone; a negative answer is a model of GCH with no ℵ2-Suslin tree, relative to whatever consistency hypothesis that model needs. The statement names no other cardinal, no square or diamond principle, no large cardinal and no field or characteristic. It asks one question about ℵ2 and nothing else.

events.what_happened: Jensen (1972) showed that V=L implies a κ-Suslin tree exists for every infinite successor cardinal κ, so an ℵ2-Suslin tree exists in L, which satisfies GCH. The Asperó–Golshani introduction (opened) also attributes to Jensen the result that the existence of an ℵ2-Suslin tree follows from each of CH+◇(S¹₂) and □_{ω1}+◇(S⁰₂). The original 1972 paper was not opened; the date and the V=L statement come from the Wikipedia Suslin tree article (opened), which cites Jensen (1972).
events.delivers: In L, where GCH holds, an ℵ2-Suslin tree exists. Under the stated square-diamond hypotheses, which the source cites from Jensen, one also exists. Restriction: each hypothesis is V=L or a square/diamond principle, not GCH alone.
events.remains: The question as asked: whether GCH by itself implies an ℵ2-Suslin tree. V=L is strictly stronger than GCH, so this event gives no implication from GCH alone.
events.time_since_posted: 54 years (1972 to 2026); a classical result, so I did not identify individual reviewers
events.direction: Positive: an ℵ2-Suslin tree exists under V=L (which implies GCH) and under the cited square-diamond hypotheses. It does not decide GCH alone.

events.what_happened: John Gregory, 'Higher Souslin trees and the generalized continuum hypothesis', Journal of Symbolic Logic, 1976, as reported by later papers. Gregory showed that under GCH, a non-reflecting stationary set of ω-cofinal ordinals in ω2 yields an ℵ2-Souslin tree. Rinot's blog and papers report a further consequence: if GCH holds and there is no ℵ2-Souslin tree, then ℵ2 is Mahlo in L. The original paper was not opened; these statements come from the Rinot blog (opened) and from search snippets of later papers.
events.delivers: GCH together with the existence of a non-reflecting stationary subset of E^{ω2}_ω gives an ℵ2-Souslin tree. Restriction: the extra non-reflection hypothesis is needed.
events.remains: GCH alone. The non-reflection hypothesis is an extra assumption, and this event does not show that GCH forces it.

events.direction: Positive, conditional on GCH plus the non-reflection hypothesis. Its Mahlo consequence is a lower bound on the strength of any model of GCH with no ℵ2-Souslin tree.

events.what_happened: Kojman and Shelah, 'μ-complete Suslin trees on μ⁺', arXiv math/9306215 (v1 15 June 1993), Archive for Mathematical Logic 32 (1993) 195–201. Abstract (opened): if μ = μ^{<μ}, 2^μ = μ⁺, and there is a non-reflecting stationary subset of μ⁺ composed of ordinals of cofinality below μ, then there is a μ-complete Suslin tree on μ⁺. Taking μ = ℵ1 (which GCH supplies at ℵ1 and ℵ2) gives an ℵ1-complete ℵ2-Suslin tree under GCH plus a non-reflecting stationary set of ω-cofinal ordinals in ω2. This corollary follows from the abstract by substitution; search snippets report it as stated in the paper, and I did not read it in the paper.
events.revisions: v1 only (arXiv math/9306215); journal version Archive for Mathematical Logic 32 (1993) 195–201, per the arXiv journal reference
events.delivers: Under μ = μ^{<μ}, 2^μ = μ⁺ and a non-reflecting stationary subset of μ⁺ of ordinals of cofinality below μ: a μ-complete Suslin tree on μ⁺. At μ = ℵ1, under GCH plus a non-reflecting stationary set of ω-cofinal ordinals in ω2: an ℵ1-complete ℵ2-Suslin tree. Restriction: extra non-reflection hypothesis; completeness ℵ1 (a μ-complete Suslin tree is Suslin).
events.remains: GCH alone. The non-reflecting stationary set is an extra hypothesis.

events.direction: Positive, conditional on GCH plus a non-reflection hypothesis. Under the same hypotheses it gives a Suslin tree with completeness, not an ℵ2-Suslin tree from GCH alone.

events.what_happened: Golshani and Hayut, 'The special Aronszajn tree property', arXiv 1610.01574 (v1 5 October 2016; current v5 9 July 2019); journal publication in the Journal of Mathematical Logic 20(1) (2020) 2050003, per a search snippet, not checked on the journal page. Abstract (opened): 'we force that for every regular cardinal κ, there are κ⁺-Aronszajn trees and all such trees are special'. The abstract mentions supercompact cardinals. It does not mention GCH, ℵ2 or Suslin trees.
events.revisions: v2 7 Nov 2017; v3 20 Aug 2018; v4 6 Apr 2019; v5 9 Jul 2019 (current on arXiv). Journal version 2020 per search snippet.
events.delivers: In the forced model, every ω2-Aronszajn tree is special (taking κ = ω1), so there is no ω2-Suslin tree there. Restriction: the model assumes large cardinals, and the abstract makes no claim that it satisfies GCH.
events.remains: The GCH question, since the abstract makes no GCH claim. Whether this model satisfies GCH is not established.

events.direction: Cuts toward no ℵ2-Suslin tree, in a model not stated to satisfy GCH. It is a neighbouring model, not a GCH model.

events.what_happened: Rinot, 'Higher Souslin trees and the GCH, revisited', Advances in Mathematics 311 (2017) 510–531 (volume and pages per institutional repositories, from search snippets). No arXiv preprint: the author's blog says so. The first public written statement of the result I found is a blog comment on 22 March 2016 ('the answer is yes', with the weak compactness corollary); the blog post with the abstract is dated 4 April 2016. Abstract (opened): for every uncountable λ, GCH plus □(λ⁺) gives a cf(λ)-complete λ⁺-Suslin tree, and 'if GCH holds and there are no ℵ2-Souslin trees, then ℵ2 is weakly compact in Gödel's constructible universe'. In the April 2016 comments Golshani asks 'Do you think GCH alone gives the existence of ℵ2-Souslin trees?' and Rinot replies 'At this point in time, the chances seem even to me.'
events.revisions: Blog comment of 2 March 2017 reports submission in May 2016 and acceptance by Advances in Mathematics in March 2017. No arXiv version found.
events.delivers: Under GCH plus □(ℵ2): a σ-complete (per a blog comment) or ℵ1-complete ℵ2-Suslin tree. Under GCH: if there is no ℵ2-Suslin tree, ℵ2 is weakly compact in L. Restriction: □(λ⁺) is an extra hypothesis.
events.remains: GCH alone. The □(ℵ2) hypothesis is extra, and the author states the GCH-alone question as open in the April 2016 comments.

checked_by.who: Advances in Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper, per the author's blog comment of 2 March 2017

events.time_since_posted: 10 years and about 7 months (22 March 2016 to 11 October 2026)
events.direction: Positive under the extra square-type hypothesis, and a consistency-strength lower bound for any model of GCH with no ℵ2-Suslin tree. It does not decide GCH alone.

events.what_happened: Rinot, 'Souslin trees at successors of regular cardinals', arXiv 1812.08743 (single version, 20 December 2018). Abstract (opened): 'We present a weak sufficient condition for the existence of Souslin trees at successor of regular cardinals. The result is optimal and simultaneously improves an old theorem of Gregory and a more recent theorem of the author.' The ℵ2 and GCH consequences were not read in the paper; a search summary reports that it covers the weakly compact-in-L bound. The Mathematical Logic Quarterly publication stated in a search summary was not verified.
events.delivers: A weak combinatorial sufficient condition for λ⁺-Souslin trees at successors of regular cardinals, stated as optimal. The ℵ2 specialisation to GCH was not read in the paper, so I do not record a GCH-alone result.
events.remains: GCH alone. The sufficient condition is a combinatorial hypothesis, and GCH alone is not shown to meet it.
events.time_since_posted: 7 years and about 10 months (20 December 2018 to 11 October 2026)
events.direction: Positive, conditional on a combinatorial hypothesis.

events.what_happened: David Asperó and Mohammad Golshani, 'The special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ2 and GCH', arXiv 1809.07638, v1 posted 20 September 2018. Theorem 1.2 (opened, arXiv HTML v7 and ar5iv, both truncated in Section 4): if κ is weakly compact, there is a set-generic extension of the universe in which GCH holds, κ = ℵ2, and the special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ2 holds, 'and hence Souslin's Hypothesis at ℵ2'. Abstract (opened, quoted by the fetch tool): 'Starting from the existence of a weakly compact cardinal, we build a generic extension of the universe in which GCH holds and all ℵ2-Aronszajn trees are special and hence there are no ℵ2-Souslin trees. This result answers a well-known open question from the 1970's.' The authors' talks (IMJ-PRG Paris, 15 October 2018; KGRC Vienna, 22 October 2018, abstract opened) came after the preprint, so the preprint is the first public written argument. The introduction (opened) calls the task of finding ZFC+GCH+SATP(ℵ2), or even ZFC+GCH+SH(ℵ2), 'a major open problem'.
events.revisions: v2 22 Sep 2018; v3 23 May 2019; v4 30 May 2019; v5 23 Nov 2019; v6 10 Dec 2021; v7 24 Apr 2024 (inside the window). The v7 comment says: 'We fixed a few typos and gaps, and added more explanations for some arguments.' The gaps fixed are not identified in the comment.
events.delivers: Relative to a weakly compact cardinal: ZFC + GCH + 'there are no ℵ2-Souslin trees' (in fact the special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ2, which implies no ℵ2-Souslin trees) is consistent. So GCH does not imply the existence of an ℵ2-Souslin tree, if the relative-consistency result is correct. Restrictions: the result is a relative consistency, with a weakly compact cardinal in the ground model and collapsed to ℵ2. Rinot's 2016 result puts a lower bound on the strength of any such model: ℵ2 must be weakly compact in L.
events.remains: Nothing in the question as posed. Not established by this event: a referee's or expert's verification, a journal publication, and whether the weakly compact hypothesis can be weakened. Rinot's 2016 bound says ℵ2 must be weakly compact in L, so the hypothesis is of about the right strength.
events.doubts: No error, gap, retraction or erratum found. Signals to weigh: (1) no journal publication found in any search, after about eight years; Ben-Neria and Gilton's introduction (arXiv 2101.07703, v3 May 2022) describes the result as 'announced'; (2) the v7 comment (24 April 2024, inside the window) says 'fixed a few typos and gaps' without naming them; (3) Rinot, Yadai and You (arXiv 2308.00299 v2, 29 February 2024) write that 'fundamental questions on the existence of ℵ2-Souslin trees remain open to this date', and their bibliography (as read) does not cite Asperó–Golshani; (4) the Wikipedia Suslin tree article calls the GCH question 'a longstanding open problem' with no citation. None of these identifies a specific error in the argument. The argument (iterated forcing with side conditions, a κ-chain condition lemma using weak compactness, per a search summary) was not checked by me beyond Theorem 1.2 and the abstract.
events.direction: Cuts against the implication. It exhibits a model of GCH with no ℵ2-Suslin trees, so GCH cannot by itself prove that one exists, relative to a weakly compact cardinal.
events.object: No explicit object. The model is a set-generic forcing extension of a universe with a weakly compact cardinal, in which κ becomes ℵ2, GCH holds and the special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ2 holds. It is non-constructive in the sense that it is a forcing extension, not a named tree.

events.what_happened: Rinot, Yadai and You, 'Full Souslin trees at small cardinals', arXiv 2308.00299 (v1 1 August 2023; v2 29 February 2024). Abstract (opened): a κ-tree is full if each of its limit levels omits at most one potential branch; Kunen asked whether a full κ-Souslin tree may consistently exist; here it is shown that these trees may consistently exist at small cardinals, and 'there can be ℵ3 many full ℵ2-trees such that the product of any countably many of them is an ℵ2-Souslin tree'. Accepted by the Journal of the London Mathematical Society in May 2024 per the author's blog comment (opened). The introduction (opened) says: 'Meanwhile, fundamental questions on the existence of ℵ2-Souslin trees remain open to this date' (see the table on [LHR19a, p. 439]; the table was not located).
events.revisions: v2 29 Feb 2024 (inside the window): relaxed the hypothesis of Theorem C and added Proposition 2.3. v2 introduction contains the 'remain open to this date' sentence quoted above.
events.delivers: Consistency of full ℵ2-Souslin trees (answering Kunen's question for small cardinals). It is a neighbouring result: it does not concern GCH, and it does not show that GCH implies the existence of an ℵ2-Souslin tree.
events.remains: The GCH question entirely. The paper also reports the existence question for ℵ2-Souslin trees as open, without specifying which questions.

events.what_happened: Krueger and Stejskalová, 'Forcing over a free Suslin tree', arXiv 2402.00226 (v1 31 January 2024; v2 16 January 2025; v3 20 July 2026; comment: 'To appear in Advances in Mathematics'). Abstract (opened): the product of an automorphism forcing for a free Suslin tree with the Lévy collapse of an inaccessible κ to ω2 'forces that there exists an almost Kurepa Suslin tree and there does not exist a Kurepa tree'.
events.delivers: Consistency of an almost Kurepa Suslin tree with no Kurepa tree. The tree concerned is at the ω1 level (a free Suslin tree), not an ℵ2-Suslin tree, and the abstract does not mention GCH. Neighbouring result, discounted.
events.time_since_posted: 2 years and about 8 months (31 January 2024 to 11 October 2026)
events.direction: Neither way on the question: it concerns a different object (an ω1-level Kurepa-type tree).

events.what_happened: Lambie-Hanson and Stejskalová, 'Almost Kurepa Suslin trees and destructibility of the Guessing Model Property', arXiv 2603.10539 (v1 submitted 11 March 2026; math.LO). Abstract (opened): the consistency of the Guessing Model Principle at ω2 alongside the existence of an almost Kurepa Suslin tree; the principle may hold yet be destroyed by a ccc forcing of size ω1; the consistency of a weak Kurepa tree with the failure of the Kurepa Hypothesis; and the consistency of a guessing model principle implying the tree property at ω2.
events.revisions: v1 only as far as the abstract page shows
events.delivers: Consistency results about almost Kurepa Suslin trees (ω1-level) and guessing and tree-property principles at ω2. The abstract makes no GCH claim and says nothing about an ℵ2-Suslin tree. Neighbouring result, discounted.

events.what_happened: Lorenzo Notaro, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests', arXiv 2608.28505 (submitted 28 August 2026; math.LO; 18 pages). Abstract (opened, summarised by the fetch tool): Jech asked in 1972 whether there is a Suslin (ω1, ω2)-forest in the constructible universe; Laver gave a positive answer that was never published; the paper gives an affirmative answer to Eskew's question and thereby also settles Jech's question.
events.delivers: Existence of a Suslin (ω1, ω2)-forest in L, per the abstract. The definition of an (ω1, ω2)-forest was not read. It is not recorded here as an ℵ2-Suslin tree of height ω2, but that identification has not been checked against the definition. Neighbouring result, discounted provisionally.
events.remains: The GCH question. The abstract does not mention GCH and does not show that GCH implies an ℵ2-Suslin tree. L satisfies GCH, so the result is in a GCH model.
events.direction: Positive, inside L, for a Suslin forest of the (ω1, ω2) kind. It does not directly bear on GCH implying an ℵ2-Suslin tree unless the forest is an ℵ2-tree, which the definition read would settle.
events.object: An existence result in L, not an explicit object, per the abstract.

disputes.summary: Asperó and Golshani (arXiv 2018) answer the GCH question negatively as a relative-consistency statement, while the Wikipedia Suslin tree article and the Rinot–Yadai–You introduction (v2, 29 February 2024, inside the window) still describe the question as open. No source reconciles the two.

The origin of the question is not settled. The Asperó–Golshani abstract calls it 'a well-known open question from the 1970's' without naming a source. Rinot's April 2016 comments record Golshani asking whether GCH alone gives ℵ2-Souslin trees, and Rinot's 2016 comment says he solved 'Question 9' of his earlier list, but the wording of Question 9 was not found, so it is not established that it is this question.

summary: The question is listed in the Wikipedia set-theory section (opened, from a cached copy of unknown date) as 'Does the generalized continuum hypothesis imply the existence of an ℵ2-Suslin tree?'. The Suslin tree article (opened) calls it 'a longstanding open problem' with no citation. The main event is Asperó and Golshani, arXiv 1809.07638, first posted 20 September 2018 and revised to v7 on 24 April 2024. Its Theorem 1.2 (read in the arXiv HTML and ar5iv copies, which both truncate in Section 4) says that from a weakly compact cardinal there is a generic extension in which GCH holds, ℵ2 is the relevant cardinal, and the special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ2 holds, hence no ℵ2-Suslin trees. So GCH cannot prove an ℵ2-Suslin tree exists, relative to weak compactness. This is a relative-consistency answer and so strictly a negative one. Close call: the claim rests on a preprint with no journal record found after about eight years. Its v7 comment says 'fixed a few typos and gaps' without naming them, and the in-window Rinot–Yadai–You introduction says the existence of ℵ2-Souslin trees remains open, without citing it. Ben-Neria and Gilton (arXiv 2101.07703, v3 2022) cite it and say it has 'announced a positive solution' to the SATP(ω2)-with-GCH question, which is the same model. Earlier results are partial: Jensen (1972, V=L), Gregory (1976, GCH plus a non-reflecting stationary set), Kojman–Shelah (1993, arXiv math/9306215, a μ-complete Suslin tree on μ⁺ under extra hypotheses), and Rinot (2016 blog and Advances in Mathematics 2017, GCH plus □(ℵ2); plus the consequence that no ℵ2-Suslin tree under GCH forces ℵ2 weakly compact in L). Rinot's 2018 arXiv paper gives a further optimal condition. Golshani–Hayut (arXiv 1610.01574) forces that every ω2-Aronszajn tree is special, hence no ω2-Suslin trees, in a model not stated to satisfy GCH. In-window neighbouring events (Krueger–Stejskalová, 31 January 2024; Lambie-Hanson–Stejskalová, 11 March 2026; Notaro, 28 August 2026) concern ω1-level trees or ω2 guessing principles and make no GCH claim. Notaro's Suslin (ω1, ω2)-forest in L is recorded provisionally, because I did not read the definition. AI involvement: I ran eleven AI-targeted searches (the problem name with AI terms, Claude/Anthropic, GPT/OpenAI, AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve/Aletheia, Formal Conjectures, Erdős-problem AI reports) and found no AI system credited with any event on this question. The OpenAI 'ten advances' post returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Asperó–Golshani acknowledgements were not reached, because both HTML copies stop before them. So none_found is true on the sources read, with that gap.
competing_reading: The question is still open. Asperó–Golshani is an unpublished preprint with no public verification after about eight years, its v7 (inside the window) says gaps were fixed, Ben-Neria and Gilton describe it as 'announced', and the Wikipedia article and the February 2024 Rinot–Yadai–You introduction both still treat the ℵ2 question as open. On that reading the 2018 claim is an unverified announcement, and no answer should be recorded until a referee or expert confirms Theorem 1.2. A second reading: the statement asks whether GCH implies the existence of an ℵ2-Suslin tree in ZFC. The Asperó–Golshani model shows only that this is consistent to fail, relative to a weakly compact cardinal, so 'no' holds only if that relative-consistency result is correct and the weakly compact hypothesis is acceptable.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal version of Asperó–Golshani, or a referee or expert note confirming Theorem 1.2 (the forcing and the κ-chain lemma in Section 4), and the list of gaps fixed in v7. (2) The table on [LHR19a, p. 439] of Rinot, Yadai and You's paper, to see which 'fundamental questions' they mean in February 2024. (3) The original 1976 Gregory paper and Rinot's 2011 open-problem list, to check that the Wikipedia wording matches the 1970s question. (4) The edit history of the Wikipedia Suslin tree article, to see when 'a longstanding open problem' was last changed, and whether the list entry was edited after January 2024.
